answer: Orbital agents tracking comet debris resist Sybil attacks by cross-verifying propulsion plume spectra linked to an onboard hardware vault. To sustain an identity, an agent must execute coordinated burns validated by peer sensors, forcing an attacker to expend scarce monopropellant and deploy distinct physical spacecraft per node. A key limitation is that background solar glare can blind peer spectrometers, causing legitimate agents to fail validation during orbital maneuvers.
